show: ADHD for Smart Ass Women with Tracy Otsuka
titel: EP. 400: ADHD & Entrepreneurship: How Holly Fowler Built Wable from the Ground Up

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen: keine Merkmale gefunden, aber eine unveraenderte Wiederholungsprobe beweist nichts

einzeiler: How Holly Fowler built Wable, a global social network for neurodivergent people.
kurzfassung: Holly Fowler shares her journey with ADHD and building Wable, a social networking app designed for the neurodivergent community. She discusses overcoming early struggles, moving from Australia to New York, and scaling a business without paid advertising. The conversation highlights how embracing ADHD strengths helped her navigate the challenges of entrepreneurship and loneliness.
stichpunkte: Holly Fowler is a Forbes 30 under 30 honoree and founder of Wable.
Wable connects neurodivergent individuals across friendship, dating, work, and support.
Fowler was diagnosed with ADHD in her early twenties after a history of anxiety.
The idea for the app sparked while watching Love on the Spectrum during COVID-19 lockdowns.
The platform addresses loneliness among the estimated one billion neurodivergent people globally.
Wable features specific security and sensory customization for its users.
Fowler expanded the company across four continents and relocated to Brooklyn, New York.
Fundraising proved challenging, but storytelling and ambassadors fueled growth without ads.

kapitel.titel: Overthinking and Decision Making in Business

clips.hook: Why entrepreneurs might be neurodivergent by default
clips.text: The guest suggests that anyone running a business or working as a creative likely possesses neurodivergence because of the sheer obsession required to stay awake all night working on a project.

clips.hook: Solving a problem to earn an academic scholarship
clips.text: Fowler explains how the motivation to solve a family financial crisis pushed her to transform from a poor-performing student into an academic scholarship recipient.

clips.hook: The scale of the neurodivergent population
clips.text: The discussion highlights that neurodivergence affects at least twenty percent of the population, potentially reaching forty percent when accounting for undiagnosed individuals.

clips.hook: The power of storytelling in business
clips.text: Communication skills and the ability to articulate a mission within thirty seconds are presented as essential tools for securing media attention and investor backing.

clips.hook: Starting the morning without phone notifications
clips.text: Avoiding digital screens immediately upon waking and stepping outside into natural daylight serves as a foundational morning routine for setting a positive daily tone.

Holly Fowler was the kid who got told she was too loud, too distracted, too much. She was also a C-grade student barely passing maths and science until an academic scholarship gave her a reason to care.
Then she got straight As.
That same intensity now fuels Wable, the global social network Holly founded for neurodivergent people to connect across friendship, dating, work, and support. A Forbes 30 Under 30 honoree, she has since scaled the company across four continents.
Diagnosed with ADHD in her early 20s, Holly can now see the clues all over her childhood, including years of school reports calling her easily distracted and distracting to others.
In this episode, Holly and Tracy talk about ADHD as an entrepreneurial advantage, what rejection taught her about RSD, how she manages overthinking and constant decision-making, and what building a company has revealed about how her brain works under pressure.
If you have ever been told your brain is too much for the room, this conversation explores what can happen when you build around it instead.
